question: A 24-year-old man presents to the emergency department complaining of a prolonged course of diarrhea. He reports that he has had 3–4 large volume watery stools daily for the last several weeks. He has no pain with bowel movements, no abdominal pain, and no blood in his stools. He is homeless and uses recreational drugs. He also reports that he usually drinks a half-liter of whiskey, or whatever else he can find, every day and he has done this for several years. The physical exam is notable for a hyperpigmented rash across his face, neck, chest, and the backs of his hands and forearms. On mental status exam, he is oriented to person and place but not time; he scores a 23/30 on the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MOCA). This patient's presentation is most likely related to which of the following micronutrients?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Chronic alcohol use" -> "poor dietary intake" -> "niacin deficiency" -> "pellagra symptoms" -> "diarrhea, dermatitis, dementia" -> "Vitamin B3" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Homelessness" -> "limited access to balanced diet" -> "niacin deficiency" -> "pellagra symptoms" -> "diarrhea, dermatitis, dementia" -> "Vitamin B3" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Prolonged diarrhea" -> "malabsorption" -> "nutrient deficiencies" -> "niacin deficiency" -> "pellagra symptoms" -> "Vitamin B3" -> 85%
analysis: The patient's symptoms and history suggest a deficiency in Vitamin B3 (niacin). The key features include prolonged diarrhea, a hyperpigmented rash in sun-exposed areas, and cognitive impairment, which are characteristic of pellagra. Pellagra is caused by niacin deficiency and is often seen in individuals with poor nutrition, such as those with alcohol use disorder. The combination of diarrhea, dermatitis, and dementia aligns with the classic triad of pellagra.
